title: How to Stop the AI-pocalypse
gist: Teaser: Kaushik Basu argues the real AI danger may be the end of democracy via concentrated power rather than (or as well as) human extinction; slowing AI likely fails amid corporate and national races, so he proposes international coordination and taxing extreme AI-generated wealth.

insights.claim: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity, by putting unprecedented power in the hands of a tiny elite.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Concentration of AI-driven wealth is a political flashpoint that invites redistribution and regulation.
insights.quote: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity
insights.locator: AI could very well end democracy

insights.claim: Efforts to slow AI development may fail because companies and countries are racing to stay ahead.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Race dynamics imply continued heavy AI capex and weak prospects for development moratoria.
insights.quote: efforts to slow its development may fail as companies and countries race to stay ahead
insights.locator: AI could very well end democracy

themes.theme: Policy response: coordination and wealth taxes

insights.claim: Preventing an AI-driven authoritarian future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth AI could create.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Signals intellectual momentum behind wealth taxes targeting AI winners, a risk for concentrated tech fortunes and valuations.
insights.quote: Preventing such a future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth
insights.locator: AI could very well end democracy

insights.claim: The digital revolution has raised living standards but has also deepened social divisions and destabilized politics around the world.
insights.speaker: Project Syndicate
insights.so_what: Tech-driven social instability feeds political risk and regulatory backlash.
